title: test(segment): pin graph_inline_storage HNSW build to 1 CPU and seed 42
body:
## Problem

`test_graph_inline_storage_contract::case_3_u8` (Uint8 + Mmap) is flaky in CI. The assertion at line 277 (`common + 2 >= TOP`, TOP=10) needs 8 of the 10 exact nearest neighbors in the approximate result. The reported failure on 2026-09-24 had only 6 in common:

```
[103, 132, 161, 288, 347, 366, 473, 543, 565, 595] vs [132, 153, 161, 173, 366, 432, 473, 543, 565, 595]
```

## Root cause

The input vectors are already seeded (`StdRng::seed_from_u64(4242)`), but the HNSW graph built for the indexed segment is not deterministic. `build_indexed` calls `SegmentBuilder::build_for_test`, which does two things:

- It passes `ResourcePermit::dummy(get_num_indexing_threads(0))`, so the permit covers every CPU on the machine. The graph build pool is sized from `permit.num_cpus` (`lib/segment/src/index/hnsw_index/hnsw/build.rs:146`), not from `max_indexing_threads` in the test config. Setting that field to 1 does not make the build single-threaded.
- It uses an unseeded `rand::rng()`, and point levels are drawn from that RNG (`build.rs:161`).

So the graph changes from run to run and from runner to runner. For the Uint8 case the recall margin is small enough that some graphs miss the threshold.

My first version of this PR pinned `max_indexing_threads` to 1. That was wrong for the reason above, and it is reverted here.

## Fix

`build_indexed` now calls `SegmentBuilder::build` directly with `ResourcePermit::dummy(1)` and `StdRng::seed_from_u64(42)`. With one CPU and a fixed seed, the graph is the same on every run. `max_indexing_threads` is back to 2, as on `dev`.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p segment --test integration graph_inline_storage_test::test_graph_inline_storage_contract`: all 6 cases pass.
- I ran `case_3_u8` 20 times with the fix on a GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` runner: 20 passed, 0 failed.
- For reference, the unfixed test also passed 20/20 on the same runner, so the flake did not show up on that machine. The fix removes both sources of variation rather than relying on the failure rate being low.
- `cargo +nightly fmt --all --check`: clean.

## Scope

Test-only change. No production code touched.

Fixes #10774

title: Reject text index with min_token_len greater than max_token_len
body:
## Summary

Fixes #10578 — a full-text index configured with `min_token_len > max_token_len` is accepted by both REST and gRPC, but the token filter then rejects every token, silently building an empty index.

This change rejects the inverted range at validation time, mirroring the existing integer-index `lookup`/`range` check.

## Changes

- **`lib/segment/src/data_types/index.rs`**: add `validate_text_index_params` and a `Validate` impl for `TextIndexParams`.
- **`lib/segment/src/types.rs`**: wire `TextIndexParams::validate` into `PayloadSchemaParams::validate` (REST path).
- **`lib/api/src/grpc/validate.rs`**: add a `Validate` impl for the gRPC `TextIndexParams` and call it from `IndexParams::validate`.
- **`lib/edge/ffi/src/payload_index.rs`**: enforce the same rule in the FFI conversion (returns `InvalidArgument`).
- **Tests**: unit test for `validate_text_index_params` and an OpenAPI regression test asserting a 422 with the new error message.

## Testing

- Unit test covers valid (`min < max`, `min == max`, unset) and invalid (`min > max`) cases.
- OpenAPI test asserts `PUT /collections/{name}/index` with `min_token_len: 10, max_token_len: 5` returns 422.

Note: I was unable to run `cargo test` locally (no Rust toolchain installed), so CI will need to confirm compilation and tests.

title: Honor `exact` in Edge facet
body:
Follow-up to #10778, which found this while comparing each Edge read method with the server.

Edge `facet` ignored `exact`. It always added up the counts reported by each segment, and nothing at the segment level reads the flag. The server's local shard (`collection/src/shards/local_shard/facet.rs`) handles `exact: true` by collecting unique values across segments, then counting each value through `read_filtered` over all segments with the ids deduplicated. A point stored in several segments in different versions is then counted once.

Edge now does the same:
- It collects `unique_values` from every segment.
- It counts each value with the existing exact `count` (a `BTreeSet` of ids across segments) under `filter AND key == value`.
- It returns the top `limit` values via `FacetResponse::top_hits`.

### Test
`exact_facet_counts_filtered_values` checks the counts, `limit` and `filter` on the exact path. It doesn't fail on the old code: on a settled Edge shard the approximate and exact counts are the same. They only differ while a point is in two segments at once, during optimization, which is hard to set up in a unit test.

title: [AI] fix(collection): saturate offset+limit in query pagination instead of overflowing (#10501)
body:
Fixes #10501.

`offset=1, limit=usize::MAX` on `/points/query` silently returned an empty page instead of the remaining points. The collection-level merge sized its take as `offset + limit`, which wraps to a tiny value on overflow instead of erroring or saturating - `lib/shard/src/query/planned_query.rs` already guarded the identical per-shard computation with `saturating_add`, but that guard didn't reach the collection-level merge boundaries.

I opened #10504 for this earlier and closed it myself once CodeRabbit's review pointed out the fix only covered the reported code path and missed a second overflow in the same file (`search.rs`'s `sum_limits`/`sum_offsets`/`require_transfers` payload-transfer heuristic). Picking it back up: fixed that spot, then wrote a regression test against `core_search_batch` (the batch-search path, not just `/points/query`) to check for more, and it caught two more overflow panics one after another - `shard/search.rs`'s `BatchSearchParams` construction, then `collection_manager/segments_searcher.rs`'s per-segment take-count map. At that point I grepped the whole workspace for the same `offset + limit` / `limit + offset` pattern and found two more untested ones: `collection/query.rs`'s auto-sharding subsampling threshold, and `edge/read_view/ops/search.rs`'s `BatchResultAggregator` sizing. All six are now `saturating_add`/`saturating_mul`, matching the existing shard-level idiom. None of this changes behavior for ordinary requests - saturating arithmetic is a no-op until the sum would actually exceed `usize::MAX`.

Tests added: extended the existing `query_prefetch_offset_limit.rs` regression test with a batch-search case (`offset=1, limit=usize::MAX` via the `#[cfg(feature = "testing")]` `search()` helper), alongside the original `/points/query` case.

### Testing
Ran the full `collection` crate test suite (265 tests, 0 failed) in a `rust:1-bookworm` container, plus `cargo clippy -p collection -p shard --lib --tests -- -D warnings` (clean) and `cargo +nightly fmt --check` (clean).

### Checklist
- [x] My PR targets the `dev` branch (not `master`) and my branch was created from `dev`.
- [x] Have you followed the guidelines in our Contributing document?
- [x] Have you checked to ensure there aren't other open Pull Requests for the same update/change? (superseding my own closed #10504, no others found)
- [x] Have you formatted your code locally using `cargo +nightly fmt --all`?
- [x] Have you checked your code using `cargo clippy`?
- [x] Have you written new tests for your core changes?
- [x] Have you successfully ran tests with your changes locally?

### AI disclosure
Both commits in this PR (and the earlier #10504) were written with AI assistance, tagged `[AI]` per the contributing guide.

- `[AI] fix(collection): saturate offset+limit in query pagination instead of overflowing (#10501)` - the original #10504 commit.
- `Saturate the remaining offset+limit overflow sites (#10501)` - this session's follow-up; missed the `[AI]` tag on this one, should have carried it forward from the first commit.

Prompt/approach: given the issue text and CodeRabbit's specific finding on #10504 (the `search.rs` heuristic can still overflow), fix that spot, then write a regression test through the batch-search path rather than trusting the fix was complete, following overflow panics as the test surfaced them, then grep the workspace for any remaining instances of the same `offset + limit` pattern rather than stopping at the first two found. I read and verified each site's surrounding logic myself (traced the call chain manually and confirmed each swap is behavior-preserving for non-overflowing inputs) before including it.

title: Compact the payload tracker of non-appendable segments the optimizer builds
body:
Stacked on #10746. The last step of the stack: something now creates compacted trackers. Only the optimizer does, only for the payload storage of a non-appendable segment it builds, and only behind a new feature flag.

## Feature flag

`compact_logstore_tracker`, implied by `serverless_compatible`. Not enabled by `all`, like `append_only_storages`, which it needs to have any effect (only append-only Blobstore storages have this tracker). Gates creation only: both formats are always readable. `openapi.json` regenerated.

## Blobstore::make_immutable

Switches to a layout for a storage that is complete and only read from now on. In the append-only mode:

- builds the compacted tracker in memory from the append-only one: unflushed mappings from RAM, flushed ones read from `log_tracker.dat`;
- swaps it in (dropping the append-only file handle) and removes `log_tracker.dat`;
- the next flush saves `compacted_tracker.dat`, after the page data as always.

Between `make_immutable` and that flush the storage on disk has no tracker file and cannot be opened, which the docs state and a test pins down. That suits a storage being built: the optimizer calls it right before its own flush of a segment in the temp directory, which a crash discards anyway. The mutable mode is left as is; the storage stays writable either way.

Above Blobstore the method is `make_immutable` on `PayloadStorageImpl` and `PayloadStorageEnum`; the tracker stays an internal detail. (`into_immutable` would trip clippy's `wrong_self_convention`: the conversion takes `&self`, the tracker sits behind the Logstore's lock.)

## SegmentBuilder

For a non-appendable segment with the flag on, `build` calls `payload_storage.make_immutable()` before its flush. `CompactedTracker::from_tracker` no longer writes, so the flat tracker of an optimizer-built segment is never written at all: created empty, removed by the conversion.

Sparse vector storages keep the append-only tracker. Plain nearest queries score from the inverted index and never read them; recommend-style queries and `with_vector` do, but compacting would preload a mapping that is rarely used.

## CompactedTracker

- `from_tracker` builds in memory and starts dirty; the first flush saves the file.
- The fs is kept as `Arc<dyn TrackerFs>`, an object-safe trait over `atomic_save`, instead of a boxed closure.

## Tests

- `test_make_immutable_is_persisted_by_flush`: nothing compacted on disk after the conversion, the append-only file is gone; after the flush a reader sees every put, flushed before or not; the storage stays writable.
- `test_make_immutable_needs_a_flush`: without the flush the storage does not open.
- `test_make_immutable_leaves_mutable_mode_alone`.
- `optimizer_makes_non_appendable_payload_storage_immutable` (segment, `append_only_storages` binary with `serverless_compatible`): a non-appendable build has `payload_storage/compacted_tracker.dat` and the sparse storage keeps its `log_tracker.dat`; payloads and sparse vectors survive a reload; an appendable build keeps both trackers append-only. Fails with the builder call removed.

title: Report the RAM of compacted payload trackers in memory usage
body:
Stacked on #10748. A compacted tracker holds every value mapping on the heap and only reads its file on open, but the payload storage's memory report listed only its files, so that RAM went unreported.

## What

- `CompactedTracker::ram_usage_bytes`: `pointers.capacity() * size_of::<Option<ValuePointer>>()`.
- `TrackerEnum`, `Logstore` and `Blobstore::ram_usage_bytes`: heap RAM held beyond the page cache of the storage files. 0 for the append-only tracker and for mutable mode, which read their mappings from the files.
- `PayloadStorageImpl::ram_usage_bytes`, and the `Mmap` and `IoUring` arms of the payload storage `MemoryReporter` use `from_files_and_ram`, so the RAM lands in `ram_bytes` of the collection report. Reports that used to carry `None` now carry `Some(0)`; the aggregation treats both as 0.

## Tests

- blobstore: RAM is 0 before `make_immutable`, covers every mapping (gaps included) after it, and stays 0 in mutable mode.
- segment `optimizer_makes_non_appendable_payload_storage_immutable`: the payload storage report of a non-appendable build carries at least 16 bytes per point of extra RAM, an appendable build `Some(0)`.
- collection memory reporter tests unchanged and passing.

## Worth knowing

The in-RAM form is as large as the flat tracker file: `Option<ValuePointer>` is 16 bytes, so the 14x compression is on disk only (about 1.6 GB of RAM for a 100M-point payload storage). The compacted file itself is still listed with the payload storage's file intent, so it can count towards `expected_cache_bytes` although it is only read on open: about 1 byte per point, not worth a separate file list from `Blobstore`.

title: Open writable Logstore over either tracker format with TrackerEnum
body:
Stacked on #10745. The writable `Logstore` now holds `TrackerEnum`, so an indexed segment whose storage has a compacted tracker opens through the same writable path (`Blobstore::open`, `Logstore::open_or_create`) as any other storage.

Indexed segments never write into these storages, but there is no read-only type for them, so the mutating methods work, just unoptimized: every flush rewrites the whole compacted file.

## TrackerEnum

- `new` always creates an append-only tracker. Creating compacted trackers is left to the serverless indexers.
- `open_writable` picks the format on disk, like `open_read_only` (renamed from `open`).
- `set`, `write_pending`, `flusher(target)`, `pointer_count`, `populate`. On the compacted variant `set` goes to RAM and `write_pending` is a no-op.

## CompactedTracker

- Keeps a `Saver`, a type-erased `atomic_save` over a clone of the fs it was created or opened writable with, like `CompactStoredFlags` keeps its `S::Fs`. `open` (read-only) keeps none, and a read-only tracker with changes gets a flusher that fails.
- Typed `S::Fs` was tried first: `Logstore`'s constructors would need `&S::Fs`, and the update-only code in segment and edge is generic over its own `Fs`. Stating `Fs::AppendFile: UniversalRead<Fs = Fs>` there overflows the trait solver (it cycles with `UniversalAppend`'s bound on `Fs`), so the fs type is erased instead and no signature outside blobstore changes.
- `flusher(target)` rewrites the file from the mappings below `target`. `Logstore::flusher` records `target` before flushing the pages; the compacted copy is taken later, inside the closure, so without the cut it would persist mappings of puts made in between, pointing at value data that is not durable yet.

## Tests

- `test_writable_open_on_compacted_tracker`: through `Blobstore::open` and `Logstore::open_or_create`, puts on a compacted storage persist, the tracker stays compacted (no `log_tracker.dat` appears), and a reader sees every value.
- `test_compacted_flusher_skips_later_puts`: a put made after the flusher was created is not persisted by it. Fails without `target`: the reopen reports a mapping past the end of the page file.
- `test_read_only_tracker_flush_fails_only_when_dirty`.

## Known limitation

`BlobstoreReader::live_reload` is still a no-op for a compacted tracker, so a live reader does not see writes made to a compacted storage after it opened it. Harmless while indexed segments never write.

title: Read Logstore through either tracker format with TrackerEnum
body:
Stacked on #10737, the next step towards an immutable, in-RAM tracker for Logstore: readers can now open a storage whose tracker is compacted.

## What

`TrackerEnum<S>` in `lib/blobstore/src/tracker/tracker_enum.rs`, with variants `AppendOnly(AppendOnlyTracker<S>)` and `Compacted(CompactedTracker)`.

- `open` and `preopen` pick the variant by which file exists: `compacted_tracker.dat` wins, `log_tracker.dat` otherwise. On a `CachedFs` the existence check is answered from the cached file listing.
- `TrackerRead` forwards per variant; `iter` unifies the two iterators with `Either`.
- `files` and `clear_cache`; the compacted tracker lives in RAM and has nothing to evict.

`LogstoreReader`, `BlobstoreReader::Logstore`, and `BlobstoreView` hold `TrackerEnum<S>` instead of `AppendOnlyTracker<S>`. The writable `Logstore` is unchanged: it builds its `LogstoreView` over `AppendOnlyTracker` directly and never went through `BlobstoreView`.

## Live reload

A storage with a compacted tracker is complete and never changes, so `live_reload` and `live_preload` return early for it, pages included. The append-only path runs exactly as before. #10746 later lets the writable `Logstore` write to such a storage; a live reader does not see those writes until it reopens, which is harmless while indexed segments never write.

## CompactedTracker changes

- `exists` and `preopen`, sharing the open options with `open`.
- The file always opens with `Populate::Blocking`, whatever the storage's `populate` is. It is read whole right after opening anyway. With `Populate::No` a disk-cache prefetch only created the handle, and `open` then downloaded the file blocking in `read_whole`, which made `preopen` pointless.
- `from_tracker(fs, dir, &impl TrackerRead)` writes a compacted file holding every mapping of another tracker. Nothing in production calls it yet; the tests use it to build compacted storages.

## Tests

- `test_reader_on_compacted_tracker`: values with gaps through `get_value` and `iter`, `files`, `clear_cache`, and a no-op `live_reload`.
- `test_preopen_schedules_compacted_tracker`: preopen through `CachedFs`, delete every file the open reads, the open still succeeds.
- `test_preopen_fetches_compacted_tracker_through_disk_cache`: preopen through `CachedFs<DiskCacheFs>`, then assert via the disk cache stats that `open` downloads 0 bytes. Fails with `Populate::No` (the open fetches the tracker file).
- `test_convert_real_tracker` (ignored): converts a real `log_tracker.dat` or `tracker.dat` given by `COMPACTED_TRACKER_SOURCE` and prints the size ratio. On a 105k-mapping payload tracker the compacted file is 1.14 bytes per mapping, 14x smaller than the flat file.

## Not in this PR

Writing the compacted file from the segment builder. Nothing writes it in production yet, so `compacted` keeps its `cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code))`.

title: Add CompactedTracker: RAM-resident Logstore tracker with a compact file
body:
Stacked on #10735, the next step towards an immutable, in-RAM tracker for Logstore.

## What

`CompactedTracker` in `lib/blobstore/src/tracker/compacted/`. It keeps every mapping in RAM as `Vec<Option<ValuePointer>>` and implements `TrackerRead` from there. Opening decodes the file once; lookups never touch the disk afterwards.

Layout: `mod.rs` holds the struct with its lifecycle and write side, `format.rs` the file layout and codec, `read.rs` the `TrackerRead` impl, and `tests.rs` the tests.

## File format

Header (magic, version, count), then three columns, varints unless noted:

- **Gaps**: the number of skipped point offsets, then each one as the distance from one past the previous.
- **Lengths**: the value length of every present mapping, in blocks of 128. A block is its minimum, a `u8` bit width, and each length minus the minimum bit-packed at that width (`common::bitpacking`).
- **Exceptions**: the present mappings that do not start where the previous value ends on the same page (the first is expected at page 0, offset 0), each as its index among present mappings, its page id, and its offset.

Values are packed back to back in the append-only pages, so exceptions only occur on page rollover and the lengths carry nearly all the information. Arbitrary pointers still encode, only less compactly.

Measured on a real payload `log_tracker.dat` (105,100 mappings, values 383 to 1040 bytes): 1.14 bytes per mapping, 14x smaller than the 16-byte flat entries. An earlier LZ4-over-varints layout reached 2.05 bytes (7.8x): LZ4 finds no repeats in the lengths, which are uncorrelated (lag-1 autocorrelation 0.04). Their order-0 entropy is 0.99 bytes, so an entropy coder (xz measured 1.11) would win at most about 13% more; not worth a new dependency.

## Write side

- `set` takes any point offset, grows the vector as needed, and replaces an existing mapping. Skipped offsets read as `None`.
- A dirty flag tracks whether anything was set since the last flusher took its copy. A clean tracker gets a flusher that does nothing.
- `flusher(fs)` swaps the flag off and clones the pointers, so mappings set during a flush wait for the next one. The closure encodes the copy and replaces the file with `atomic_save`. A failed write marks the tracker dirty again, so the next flush retries. A whole-file rewrite needs a filesystem handle rather than an open file, so the flusher takes the `Fs` by value.
- Rewriting is linear in the mapping count. This suits a storage flushed once after being built, which is the intended use.

## Read side

`open` rejects a missing file the same way the other trackers do, and rejects a corrupt one: truncated header or payload, trailing bytes, bad magic or version, and columns that do not add up to valid pointers are all tested. A header count off by a few can hide in the bit padding of the last length block, so the count tests use a whole block more and zero; the flat tracker file has no checksum either.

## Not in this PR

Wiring into `Logstore`, `LogstoreReader`, and `BlobstoreReader`, and writing the file from the segment builder. The module carries `cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code))` until then.

`integer-encoding` is added to the crate. It is already a workspace dependency used by `segment`.
